findings.issue_text: [BUG] The handler calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking), a method this diff never adds to EventManager and which the repo's EventManager does not expose. The build fails with a TypeScript 'Property updateCalendarAttendees does not exist on type EventManager' error (or, if it slips through with any-casting, a runtime TypeError when any guest add is attempted), so the entire addGuests mutation is dead on arrival.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), requiring the caller to be simultaneously admin AND owner, which the membership model never satisfies for an admin who is not the owner. Team admins open the Add Guests dialog, submit, and get FORBIDDEN ('you_do_not_have_permission') because the && can never be true for them; the operator must use || as the permission check intends.

[BUG] multiEmailValue is initialized to [""], so the length===0 guard in handleAdd never fires and z.string().email() validation fails on the empty string the moment the user clicks Add on an untouched dialog. A user who opens the dialog and immediately clicks Add sees 'Emails must be unique and valid' with no way to trigger the intended empty-input no-op; the [""] sentinel also means a user who clears the last field cannot submit an empty list as intended.

[BUG] The handler passes the raw input guests (which may contain emails of already-existing attendees, duplicates, or blacklisted emails) to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of uniqueGuests, so the email branch's newGuests.includes(attendee.email) test classifies existing attendees as 'new guests'. When a caller passes an email that is already an attendee, that attendee receives a full AttendeeScheduledEmail (booking-confirmation email with ICS) instead of the AddGuests notification, re-sending confirmations to people who already booked and desynchronizing notification content from what actually changed.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, so only users who are simultaneously admin AND owner pass the check. A user who is a team admin but not the team owner (and not the organizer or an attendee) gets a FORBIDDEN error when adding guests to their team's booking — the documented access path silently fails; the auth check is stricter than the intent, and plain admins are locked out.

[BUG] The EventManager is constructed with the requesting user (`...user`, credentials from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer (`booking.user`), while evt.organizer is built from the organizer. When an attendee (a permitted non-organizer caller per the isAttendee check) adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with the attendee's credentials, so the organizer's external calendar event is never updated with the new guests (or the update crashes on missing calendar credential); only the organizer caller works.

[BUG] The guest blacklist comparison lowercases the env entries but not the guest email, so a case-varied email bypasses the filter. Blacklisting 'spam@evil.com' in BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS does not block 'Spam@Evil.com' — the blacklisted address is created as an attendee, defeating the operator-configured blacklist.

[BUG] The server-side uniqueness filter compares each guest against existing booking attendees but never deduplicates guests within the input array, while the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts z.array(z.string().email())) has no uniqueness refine unlike the client copy. A direct tRPC mutation with guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] passes the schema and creates two identical attendee rows for the same email, duplicating that guest on the booking and in every subsequent email/calendar sync; the client-only refine is not a security boundary.

[BUG] isInvalidEmail is set true on validation failure but is never reset when the user edits the emails and retries via handleAdd, and is not cleared on dialog open — only the Cancel button clears it. After one invalid submission, the 'emails must be unique and valid' error stays rendered even after the user fixes the input and clicks Add again with valid emails (validation succeeds, mutation fires, but the stale error remains until success closes the dialog), telling the user their now-valid input is still wrong.

[ADVISORY] The sendAddGuestsEmails failure is swallowed with a bare console.log that drops the error object and any stack. When SMTP or template rendering fails, guests are persisted as attendees but no one is notified and no organizer-visible error surfaces — the API still returns 'Guests added' success, and an operator triaging the incident has no error details in logs to diagnose why notifications were silently lost.

[ADVISORY] The new addGuests mutation handler — including its permission checks, blacklist filter, and attendee-creation path — ships with no test coverage anywhere in this diff (no spec/test files added or modified). The && vs || authorization bug and the case-sensitivity blacklist bypass above are exactly the regressions a handler test would have caught; the next refactor of the permission logic ships with the same blind spot and users who are wrongly FORBIDDEN (or wrongly admitted) have no test to pin the intended behavior.

[ADVISORY] The add_members menu item is added unconditionally to every booking's action list, with no gating on booking status (cancelled/rejected) or event type, unlike the surrounding items which are conditionally included. Users see 'Additional Guests' on cancelled and rejected bookings where adding guests is meaningless, and clicking it lets them add attendees to a cancelled booking's roster, generating 'guests added' emails for an event that will never occur.

[ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails sends the full AttendeeScheduledEmail to brand-new guests whose name is the empty string (handler creates attendees with name: ""), while existing attendees get the shorter AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. New guests receive a scheduling confirmation email addressed to a blank name and carrying a duplicate calendar invite (method REQUEST, status CONFIRMED) for an event they never booked; if their mail client already has the event, the blank-name invite confuses the roster, and the new guests get no indication they were added by someone else rather than having booked themselves.

[ADVISORY] Guest timezone is unconditionally set to the organizer's timezone and locale to the organizer's locale when creating guest attendee records. Every guest's stored timezone is wrong unless they happen to share the organizer's; reminder emails and ics attachments render times in the organizer's timezone/locale for guests in other regions, who receive meeting times they must mentally convert — incorrect data persisted, not just a rendering issue.

[BUG] The permission gate computes isTeamAdminOrOwner as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, requiring the caller to be BOTH admin and owner instead of either. A team admin who is not the owner, adding guests to their team's booking, receives FORBIDDEN even though the PR's own variable name and intent state admin-or-owner should be allowed; conversely the gate silently grants nothing to plain admins — the authorization check does not match its stated invariant.

[BUG] The duplicate-attendee check `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive while the blacklist comparison lowercases the list entry, so the filter is inconsistent on email case. Submitting `Guest@Example.com` when `guest@example.com` is already an attendee creates a duplicate attendee row (two ICS attendees, two emails to the same person), and `Guest@Example.com` bypasses the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blacklist because the comparison compares a raw-case guest against lowercased entries.

[BUG] The handler passes the raw input `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of the computed `uniqueGuests`. A guest who was already an attendee (or blacklisted) but included in the input list is classified as a 'new guest' in email-manager.ts (`newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`), so existing attendees receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail (a re-send of the original booking confirmation) instead of the guests-added notification.

[ADVISORY] The new BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env var silently drops emails rather than surfacing a validation error, and the filter is undisclosed to the caller. An operator sets the blacklist and an organizer adds a mixed list: some guests are silently not added while the UI shows 'Guests added', leaving the organizer with no signal that anyone was excluded; the env var itself has no documentation or schema/typing entry anywhere in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The Zod email-uniqueness schema and the handler's duplicate filter are two parallel hand-maintained validations, and the dialog resets `isInvalidEmail` only in the cancel path, never when the user fixes the input. Once the user triggers the invalid-email banner, it stays rendered after they correct the emails and successfully submit, because `isInvalidEmail` is only reset on cancel; the server-side uniqueGuests check also uses different rules (case-sensitivity) than the client schema, so the two validators drift and produce different accept/reject answers for the same input.

[ADVISORY] The 'additional_guests' menu option is added unconditionally to every booking item with no gating on booking state (past/cancelled bookings) or the user's role, even though the handler will reject FORBIDDEN for unrelated users. Users browsing bookings where they are neither organizer, attendee, nor team owner see the Add Guests action, open the dialog, enter emails, and only then receive a FORBIDDEN toast — work the diff ships that is not traceable to the intended audience of the feature.

[BUG] The team-permission check uses AND instead of OR: `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the user to be BOTH admin and owner, so a plain team admin (not owner) is correctly denied but a team owner who is not an admin is also denied, and neither can ever satisfy the intended 'admin or owner' gate. Team admins/owners who are not the booking organizer or attendee get FORBIDDEN for an operation the design intends them to perform; conversely the gate as written is stricter than specified and the boolean logic contradicts the variable name isTeamAdminOrOwner.

[BUG] Format drift between writer and comparator: blacklisted emails are lowercased (`email.toLowerCase()`) but guest emails are compared raw (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so a guest entered as `User@Example.com` never matches a blacklist entry stored as `user@example.com`. The blacklist filter silently fails to match mixed-case input, letting blacklisted addresses be added as attendees; same asymmetry applies to the existing-attendee dedup (`guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive), so `Bob@x.com` is re-added when `bob@x.com` already attends, producing duplicate attendee rows.

[BUG] Confusable-pair binding: the EventManager is constructed from the REQUESTING user (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, `...user`) instead of the booking organizer (`booking.userId`), even though the code explicitly resolved `organizer` as a separate record. When an attendee or team admin (not the organizer) adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with the caller's calendar credentials against the organizer's booking — the calendar update targets the wrong account's calendars, fails outright for users with no calendar credential, or mutates via credentials that don't own the event.

[BUG] TOCTOU duplicate creation: the dedup filter reads `booking.attendees` fetched in an earlier query, then `createMany` inserts with no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and no transaction, so two concurrent addGuests calls (or a retry after a calendar/email failure) both pass the filter and both insert. Duplicate attendee rows for the same email on one booking — duplicate emails, duplicate ICS updates, and double-counted seats for seat-based event types.

[BUG] The email routine is passed the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so the `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` branch in sendAddGuestsEmails is evaluated against emails that were filtered out (existing attendees, blacklist hits) plus raw-case strings. An already-attending email that the user retypes gets an 'AttendeeScheduledEmail' (full scheduled-booking email) instead of the guests-added email, and case-mismatched duplicates cause both email variants to be sent to the same person.

[BUG] `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` throws an unhandled Prisma P2025 when booking.userId is null (unassigned bookings exist per the `|| 0` guard the code itself writes), surfacing as a 500 instead of a 4xx. Any addGuests call on a booking with no organizer user crashes with an internal server error rather than a meaningful error, after the permission check already passed.

[BUG] The server-side schema lacks the uniqueness refine the client enforces in AddGuestsDialog (parallel client+server validation that has already drifted in this same diff), so duplicate emails within one request pass server validation and are all inserted by createMany. Any non-UI caller (API consumer) submits `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` and gets two identical attendee rows for one booking; the uniqueness invariant exists only in the discarded client copy.

[ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails pushes an OrganizerAddGuestsEmail with no teamMember (organizer) and then loops over `calendarEvent.team.members` sending one per member with no exclusion of the organizer, so the organizer receives the same email twice when they are a team member. Organizers of team bookings get duplicate 'Guests Added' notifications on every guest addition; drift risk if member list already includes the organizer by construction.

[ADVISORY] The operation is non-atomic across three side-effecting systems: attendee rows are committed via prisma.booking.update, then updateCalendarAttendees runs against external calendars, then emails are sent with a catch that only console.logs — a failure at the calendar step throws after the DB write, leaving guests persisted but unnotified and the route returning 500 for an operation that partially succeeded. Retrying after a calendar/email failure re-enters with the now-updated attendee list, and the TOCTOU gap doubles rows; users see 'unable to add guests' while guests were actually added.

[ADVISORY] The attendee path grants full guest-management to ANY attendee of ANY booking (`booking.attendees.find(a => a.email === user.email)`), an authorization scope much wider than the organizer/admin path and unverified against the booking's actual status (cancelled bookings accept new guests). Any past guest of a booking can add arbitrary emails to it indefinitely and reactivate calendar updates on cancelled events; also `booking.status` is never checked, so guests are added to CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings and send 'CONFIRMED' ICS updates for them.

[ADVISORY] The dialog's initial state `useState<string[]>([""])` means MultiEmail renders one empty EmailField, and handleAdd's only guard is `multiEmailValue.length === 0`, which is never true since the array always holds at least one string — the empty-string case falls through to the zod email check and shows the generic 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error rather than a no-op. Users clicking Add without typing anything get a validation error instead of the dialog silently doing nothing; the length-0 early return is dead code given the [""] sentinel state.

[BUG] The permission check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, so a user must be BOTH team admin AND owner to qualify, silently stripping the intended 'team admin or owner can add guests' permission from real admins and owners. A team admin (or owner who is not admin) who is neither the organizer nor an attendee of a booking gets FORBIDDEN 'you_do_not_have_permission' when adding guests, contradicting the accepted requirement that team admins/owners can manage guests on their team's bookings.

[BUG] Existing-attendee and blacklisted guest emails are silently filtered out, and if the entire submitted list is filtered the user gets a BAD_REQUEST with message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', which misreports the actual reason (blacklist or duplicate of current attendee). An organizer adds one already-invited email plus one blacklisted email: both are dropped, the user sees 'emails must be unique and valid' even though the input was unique and valid, and partial additions (some guests silently skipped) happen with no per-guest feedback.

[BUG] isInvalidEmail is set to true on validation failure but never cleared on a subsequent successful validation, so the red 'emails must be unique and valid' banner persists after the user corrects the input and while the mutation runs. A user who types one bad email, fixes it, and re-submits sees the error message remain next to valid emails, making them believe the add failed even though the mutation succeeds; the flag only resets on Cancel/Cancel-close.

[BUG] handleAdd silently returns when multiEmailValue is an empty array (which is the state after the user removes the last email row), giving no feedback at all on the Add click. A user removes the last email field and clicks Add: nothing happens, no toast, no error — a dead button with zero indication why.

[ADVISORY] The ZAddGuestsInputSchema (array of emails plus uniqueness refinement) is hand-duplicated in the dialog component instead of importing the single ZAddGuestsInputSchema from addGuests.schema.ts, creating parallel client/server schemas that can drift. A future change to the server schema (e.g., max guest count or stricter email rule) will not be reflected in the dialog, so the client will submit payloads the server rejects or block payloads the server accepts; the next editor must update two files in two packages to change one rule.

[BUG] The EventManager is constructed with ctx.user's credentials (the caller, who may be a mere attendee with no calendar integrations) and then updateCalendarAttendees is called, so the calendar update runs against the caller's credentials rather than the booking organizer's. When an attendee (the only authorized non-organizer path, since the && bug blocks admins) adds guests, eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs with the attendee's empty credentials and the organizer's Google/Outlook calendar is never updated — the new guests silently miss the calendar invite, diverging from the feature's promise that guests are added to the event.

[BUG] The sendAddGuestsEmails failure is swallowed by a bare catch that logs 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' without the error object, and the DB write to booking.attendees has already committed, so guests persist with no notification and no record of why email failed. When SMTP/calendaring email delivery fails, attendees are created in the database but nobody is emailed and the caller sees 'Guests added' success toast; the console.log drops the error object so the failure is undiagnosable in production logs.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails dispatches AttendeeScheduledEmail (a full 'you are scheduled' confirmation) to every attendee whose email is in newGuests, including the person who performed the add if they are an existing attendee, because the check compares against the raw guests array (which still contains duplicates filtered out server-side) rather than the deduplicated/filtered list actually created. An organizer who adds a guest and whose own email is an existing attendee... more importantly, guests that were filtered out as duplicates still trigger a 'scheduled' email to that existing attendee: e.g., adding an email that already matches an attendee sends that attendee a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the guests-added email, re-confirming an event to people as if they just booked.

[ADVISORY] OrganizerAddGuestsEmail wraps OrganizerScheduledEmail, whose body renders the full booking details and cancel/reschedule links context (with callToAction nulled), so the organizer-facing 'guests added' email is essentially the original scheduling email with a swapped title, while AttendeeAddGuestsEmail keeps the scheduled email's full callToAction. New attendees receive an email that looks like a brand-new booking confirmation including a cancel link whose semantics were designed for the original booker; recipients reading the email cannot tell it is a guest-add notification rather than a new event they booked, generating support noise.

[BUG] The add_members menu item is added to optionItems unconditionally for every booking in the list, with no permission gating matching the server's (organizer/admin/attendee) check. Every user viewing any booking in their list sees the 'Additional Guests' menu entry; non-authorized users click it, fill the dialog, submit, and only then hit the FORBIDDEN toast — the UI promises an action the server denies.

[BUG] The authorization check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, so a user must be BOTH the team admin AND the team owner to satisfy the team-permission branch. Any team admin who is not also the team owner is wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN, and because the same expression is the only team-based path, the gate as written either over-restricts admins or — if someone later 'fixes' the surrounding code — silently widens who can mutate any booking's attendees; as-is it is a broken authorization gate on a mutation that writes to arbitrary bookings and triggers emails/calendar updates.

[BUG] The blacklist is lowercased (BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS split and .toLowerCase()) but the incoming guest strings are compared un-normalized, so blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) is a normalization-mismatch bypass. An authorized user adds a guest with mixed case (e.g. 'Blocked@evil.com' against blacklist entry 'blocked@evil.com') and the deny rule never matches; the blacklisted email is enrolled as a booking attendee and receives the full ICS/email payload, defeating the operator-configured blacklist entirely.

[BUG] Existing-attendee dedup uses exact string equality (guest === attendee.email) while emails are not case-normalized anywhere in the schema or handler (ZAddGuestsInputSchema only checks z.string().email()). A guest already on the booking who is re-added with different case ('Jane@Example.com' vs stored 'jane@example.com') bypasses the duplicate filter and is created a second time via createMany, producing duplicate attendees who each get emailed and re-added to the calendar event.

[ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input 'guests' rather than the handler's filtered 'uniqueGuests', and the newGuests.includes(attendee.email) comparison is case-sensitive against un-normalized input. Attendees whose emails differ in case (or duplicates filtered server-side) are misclassified into the wrong email template: an existing attendee gets the 'new guest' full AttendeeScheduledEmail and a newly added guest gets only the 'guests added' notice without the full booking details; who gets bitten is every recipient of a guest-added email where case drifts between input and stored attendee records.

[ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails is wrapped in try/catch that swallows the error with a bare console.log of a static string, discarding the err object. Operators debugging why guests received no confirmation email have no error detail in logs (the thrown error is dropped, not logged), and the mutation still returns success, so failures are silent to both the user and the log trail.

[ADVISORY] The attendee-createMany and the downstream calendar/email side effects run non-atomically: prisma.booking.update commits new attendee rows before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendieves and sendAddGuestsEmails execute, with no transaction and no compensating delete. When updateCalendarAttendees throws (bad credential, calendar API failure) the handler rejects with a 500 but the guest rows are already persisted — bookings show guests who were never added to the external calendar event or emailed, and there is no remove-guests endpoint to undo them, so the data drift is permanent without manual SQL.

[ADVISORY] New attendee rows are created with name: "" and the guest's locale/timeZone copied from the organizer rather than the guest, bypassing the enrichment/validation the booking flow normally applies. Organizers receive calendar invites and emails addressing guests as empty names, and any downstream code that renders attendee names (ICS attendee CN, email templates) shows blank strings for every guest added through this path.

[ADVISORY] isTeamAdminOrOwner computes (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)), requiring the caller to be BOTH admin AND owner rather than either, so plain team admins are denied. A team admin who is not the team owner attempts to add guests to a team booking they do not organize and receives FORBIDDEN despite being an admin — the authorization gate silently rejects a class of users the UI's add_members menu item is shown to.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails failures are caught and reduced to console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") without the err object, then the handler returns success. When the email service fails, the API returns {message:"Guests added"} and the UI shows a success toast while no organizer or attendee ever receives a notification email; the error variable isn't even logged, so the failure is unobservable in production logs and permanently swallowed.

[BUG] Attendees are committed to the database (prisma.booking.update createMany) before updateCalendarAttendees and email sending run, with no rollback or compensation if either later step throws. If eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees throws (bad credential, calendar API error), the request 500s but the guests rows are already persisted; the calendar event never gains the guests and no email is sent, while the database says they were added — silent partial state with no retry path, since a retry hits the duplicate-filter and returns BAD_REQUEST.

[BUG] The dedup filter compares guest emails to existing attendees but never dedups within the input array itself (the uniqueness refine exists only in the client-side schema in AddGuestsDialog.tsx; ZAddGuestsInputSchema in addGuests.schema.ts has no uniqueness check), so duplicate guests in one request are createMany'd twice. A client that bypasses the dialog (or any direct tRPC caller) sending guests:["a@x.com","a@x.com"] creates two duplicate Attendee rows for the same booking and sends the guest two confirmation emails; the booking then permanently shows duplicated attendees.

[BUG] When uniqueGuests.length === 0 after filtering, the handler throws TRPCError BAD_REQUEST "emails_must_be_unique_valid", but that condition also covers the case where every requested guest already exists as an attendee. A user who retries after a partially-failed earlier request (attendees persisted, calendar/emails failed — see the no-rollback finding) gets 'emails must be unique and valid' even though their input is perfectly valid and unique; the wrong-shape, wrong-content error misdirects debugging and blocks the retry that would be needed to complete the calendar update and emails.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), so it is true only for users who are simultaneously admin AND owner — a team admin who is not the owner is denied, and isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0) is also evaluated for personal bookings where teamId is null. Team admins (not owners) who should be permitted to manage guests on team bookings get FORBIDDEN, and for every non-team booking the handler still runs two team-membership queries against teamId 0 on the hot path; the authorization gate does not match its evident intent (admin OR owner).

[BUG] Blacklist comparison lowercases the env-var entries but compares them against guest emails verbatim, so 'User@Example.com' does not match a blacklisted 'user@example.com'. Any guest email with different letter casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entirely and is added to the booking; the blacklist the operator configured silently fails to block, with no error surfaced.

[ADVISORY] The EventManager is constructed with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) — the requesting user's credentials — rather than the booking organizer's (booking.user.credentials is even fetched in the findFirst include and then unused). When an attendee or team admin adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs against apps the organizer's calendar lives on but with the requester's (possibly empty) credential set, so the organizer's calendar event is never updated with the new guests and the failure is invisible because the handler still returns success.

[ADVISORY] The onError toast builds `"${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}"`, a template literal that is always truthy, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never render and err.data?.code renders as the literal string 'undefined' when code is absent. Users see toasts like 'undefined: booking_not_found' — the server's raw translation key shown untranslated alongside 'undefined', misdirecting the user; the intended human-readable fallback is dead code.

[ADVISORY] Closing the dialog via Dialog onOpenChange (clicking the backdrop or Escape) resets neither multiEmailValue nor isInvalidEmail, unlike the Cancel button which resets both. A user who triggers the validation error, closes the dialog via backdrop/Escape, and reopens it sees the stale red 'Emails must be unique and valid' error and their previous emails with no way to realize the state wasn't fresh; two close paths have drifted apart.

[ADVISORY] replyTo is built by appending the organizer email plus every attendee email with no bound, so the header grows linearly with attendee count. On bookings with many attendees (large seat-based bookings, or after repeated addGuests calls), the reply-to header exceeds SMTP recipient header limits and the receiving server rejects or truncates the message, silently failing delivery of the organizer notification.

[ADVISORY] ZAddGuestsInputSchema puts no cap on the guests array length, and the handler issues one calendar-attendee update plus one email per guest with no bound. A single authenticated request with hundreds of guest emails fans out to hundreds of SMTP sends and calendar-API attendee updates from one mutation, an amplification vector that also slows the request until SMTP timeouts surface as the swallowed-email failure above; the parallel client-side schema in AddGuestsDialog.tsx duplicates the same array schema, so the two validators will drift.

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts), it always enqueues an organizer notification via `new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ calEvent: calendarEvent })`, and then, if `calendarEvent.team?.members` exists, it loops all `team.members` and enqueues `new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ calEvent: calendarEvent, teamMember })` for each member without deduplication/excluding the organizer. If the organizer is present in `calendarEvent.team.members`, they will receive two organizer emails for the same guest-add event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The operation is non-atomic across three side-effecting systems: attendee rows are committed via prisma.booking.update, then updateCalendarAttendees runs against external calendars, then emails are sent with a catch that only console.logs — a failure at the calendar step throws after the DB write, leaving guests persisted but unnotified and the route returning 500 for an operation that partially succeeded. Retrying after a calendar/email failure re-enters with the now-updated attendee list, and the TOCTOU gap doubles rows; users see 'unable to add guests' while guests were actually added.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the DB write happens first (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), then an external side effect runs (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`) with no surrounding try/catch or compensation/rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will error after persisting the new attendee rows, yielding a 500/failed response for an operation that partially succeeded (guests are added in DB but calendars/emails may not reflect it). The finding’s “doubles rows on retry” is overstated because `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendee emails on subsequent calls, but the non-atomic partial-success behavior is directly evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The attendee path grants full guest-management to ANY attendee of ANY booking (`booking.attendees.find(a => a.email === user.email)`), an authorization scope much wider than the organizer/admin path and unverified against the booking's actual status (cancelled bookings accept new guests). Any past guest of a booking can add arbitrary emails to it indefinitely and reactivate calendar updates on cancelled events; also `booking.status` is never checked, so guests are added to CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings and send 'CONFIRMED' ICS updates for them.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly allows any attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the gate is `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`—so any existing attendee can mutate the booking by adding arbitrary guest emails. The handler also never checks any booking lifecycle/status (e.g., cancelled/rejected) before updating attendees and calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. Additionally, the new email templates hardcode ICS `status: "CONFIRMED"` in both `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, so if this is invoked on a cancelled booking, it would still emit a CONFIRMED update. These behaviors are directly shown in the diff and match the finding’s security/correctness concerns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dialog's initial state `useState<string[]>([""])` means MultiEmail renders one empty EmailField, and handleAdd's only guard is `multiEmailValue.length === 0`, which is never true since the array always holds at least one string — the empty-string case falls through to the zod email check and shows the generic 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error rather than a no-op. Users clicking Add without typing anything get a validation error instead of the dialog silently doing nothing; the length-0 early return is dead code given the [""] sentinel state.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `multiEmailValue` is initialized to `[""]`, so `handleAdd`'s guard `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) return;` is effectively unreachable on the initial state. Clicking “Add” with the default empty field will fall through to Zod validation (`z.string().email()`), fail, and set `isInvalidEmail` which displays the generic `emails_must_be_unique_valid` message. This is a diff-grounded UX/logic mismatch (dead code + arguably confusing empty-submit handling), but it’s not a clear correctness defect since showing a validation error for an empty email is reasonable behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The permission check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, so a user must be BOTH team admin AND owner to qualify, silently stripping the intended 'team admin or owner can add guests' permission from real admins and owners. A team admin (or owner who is not admin) who is neither the organizer nor an attendee of a booking gets FORBIDDEN 'you_do_not_have_permission' when adding guests, contradicting the accepted requirement that team admins/owners can manage guests on their team's bookings.

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
This requires a user to be **both** a team admin and a team owner to pass the team-role permission gate. Given the name `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and typical role semantics, this is very likely incorrect and will deny access to admins who aren’t owners (and vice versa) unless they are also the organizer/attendee, triggering the `FORBIDDEN` path right below.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Existing-attendee and blacklisted guest emails are silently filtered out, and if the entire submitted list is filtered the user gets a BAD_REQUEST with message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', which misreports the actual reason (blacklist or duplicate of current attendee). An organizer adds one already-invited email plus one blacklisted email: both are dropped, the user sees 'emails must be unique and valid' even though the input was unique and valid, and partial additions (some guests silently skipped) happen with no per-guest feedback.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, submitted `guests` are filtered into `uniqueGuests` by removing (a) emails already in `booking.attendees` and (b) emails in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (see `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`). If everything is filtered out, the handler throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, which is misleading when the actual reason is “already an attendee” or “blacklisted”, not invalid/duplicate-within-input. If only some are filtered, the remaining are added via `createMany` and success is returned with no indication that some were skipped (UI always toasts `t("guests_added")`). This matches the finding’s described behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isInvalidEmail is set to true on validation failure but never cleared on a subsequent successful validation, so the red 'emails must be unique and valid' banner persists after the user corrects the input and while the mutation runs. A user who types one bad email, fixes it, and re-submits sees the error message remain next to valid emails, making them believe the add failed even though the mutation succeeds; the flag only resets on Cancel/Cancel-close.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` (new file), `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd`, but it is never reset to `false` on subsequent successful validation or before triggering the mutation. The only reset is in the Cancel button handler (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). Therefore, after a user corrects the emails and re-submits, the red error banner (`{isInvalidEmail && ...}`) will still render while the mutation is pending and until the dialog closes on success, matching the reported persistent-error behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] handleAdd silently returns when multiEmailValue is an empty array (which is the state after the user removes the last email row), giving no feedback at all on the Add click. A user removes the last email field and clicks Add: nothing happens, no toast, no error — a dead button with zero indication why.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `handleAdd` does `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) { return; }` with no toast/error/state change. The new `MultiEmail` component allows removing the last email row (`updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`), which can set the value to `[]`. In that state, clicking the "Add" button triggers `handleAdd` and silently does nothing, matching the reported dead-button behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The ZAddGuestsInputSchema (array of emails plus uniqueness refinement) is hand-duplicated in the dialog component instead of importing the single ZAddGuestsInputSchema from addGuests.schema.ts, creating parallel client/server schemas that can drift. A future change to the server schema (e.g., max guest count or stricter email rule) will not be reflected in the dialog, so the client will submit payloads the server rejects or block payloads the server accepts; the next editor must update two files in two packages to change one rule.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows client-side validation is implemented with a locally defined `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` inside `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` (an array of emails with a uniqueness refinement), while the server defines and uses a separate `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` (an object `{ bookingId, guests }` with only `email()` validation). This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/architecture issue: client and server validation rules are now split across files/packages and can drift if server-side constraints change, though it’s not a verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The EventManager is constructed with ctx.user's credentials (the caller, who may be a mere attendee with no calendar integrations) and then updateCalendarAttendees is called, so the calendar update runs against the caller's credentials rather than the booking organizer's. When an attendee (the only authorized non-organizer path, since the && bug blocks admins) adds guests, eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs with the attendee's empty credentials and the organizer's Google/Outlook calendar is never updated — the new guests silently miss the calendar invite, diverging from the feature's promise that guests are added to the event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar sync is performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `credentials` come from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (the caller). The handler separately loads the booking organizer (`organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow(...)`) but does not use the organizer’s credentials for `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. Since the permission check allows an attendee (`isAttendee`) to call this mutation, an attendee without calendar integrations would cause `updateCalendarAttendees` to run with empty/irrelevant credentials, plausibly preventing the organizer’s external calendar from being updated with the new guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sendAddGuestsEmails failure is swallowed by a bare catch that logs 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' without the error object, and the DB write to booking.attendees has already committed, so guests persist with no notification and no record of why email failed. When SMTP/calendaring email delivery fails, attendees are created in the database but nobody is emailed and the caller sees 'Guests added' success toast; the console.log drops the error object so the failure is undiagnosable in production logs.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, attendees are persisted via `prisma.booking.update(... createMany ...)` before attempting email delivery. The subsequent `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` swallows any failure, logs no error object, and still returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" };`). This means guests can be added in the DB with no emails sent, the client mutation still succeeds (showing the success toast), and production logs lack the underlying error for diagnosis.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails dispatches AttendeeScheduledEmail (a full 'you are scheduled' confirmation) to every attendee whose email is in newGuests, including the person who performed the add if they are an existing attendee, because the check compares against the raw guests array (which still contains duplicates filtered out server-side) rather than the deduplicated/filtered list actually created. An organizer who adds a guest and whose own email is an existing attendee... more importantly, guests that were filtered out as duplicates still trigger a 'scheduled' email to that existing attendee: e.g., adding an email that already matches an attendee sends that attendee a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the guests-added email, re-confirming an event to people as if they just booked.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out already-existing attendees and blacklisted emails, and only creates new attendee rows from `uniqueGuests`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (the raw input), not `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (`email-manager.ts`), the decision `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` determines who receives a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Because `newGuests` is the unfiltered `guests` array, any email the client submitted that already existed as an attendee (or was otherwise filtered out) will still match `includes(...)`, causing that existing attendee to receive a fresh `AttendeeScheduledEmail` incorrectly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OrganizerAddGuestsEmail wraps OrganizerScheduledEmail, whose body renders the full booking details and cancel/reschedule links context (with callToAction nulled), so the organizer-facing 'guests added' email is essentially the original scheduling email with a swapped title, while AttendeeAddGuestsEmail keeps the scheduled email's full callToAction. New attendees receive an email that looks like a brand-new booking confirmation including a cancel link whose semantics were designed for the original booker; recipients reading the email cannot tell it is a guest-add notification rather than a new event they booked, generating support noise.

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` the attendee email selection appears inverted: it sends `new AttendeeScheduledEmail(calendarEvent, attendee)` when `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (i.e., to newly-added guests), and sends `new AttendeeAddGuestsEmail(calendarEvent, attendee)` to everyone else (`packages/emails/email-manager.ts`). Additionally, `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` is just a thin wrapper around `AttendeeScheduledEmail` with swapped `title`/`subject` (`packages/emails/src/templates/AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.tsx`), so newly-added guests will definitely receive the full “scheduled/booking confirmation” template rather than an explicit “guests added” notification. This matches the finding’s concern that new guests get an email that reads like a new booking confirmation rather than a guest-add notice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The add_members menu item is added to optionItems unconditionally for every booking in the list, with no permission gating matching the server's (organizer/admin/attendee) check. Every user viewing any booking in their list sees the 'Additional Guests' menu entry; non-authorized users click it, fill the dialog, submit, and only then hit the FORBIDDEN toast — the UI promises an action the server denies.

adjudication.rationale: In `BookingListItem.tsx`, the new `add_members` option is appended to `optionItems` unconditionally (no checks around organizer/team role/attendee status) and always opens `AddGuestsDialog`. On the server, `addGuestsHandler` enforces permissions (`!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee` => `FORBIDDEN`). The diff therefore shows a UI/server permission mismatch: the UI advertises an action without mirroring the server gating, which can lead to a poor UX (user only learns via error toast after submission). However, from the diff alone we can’t verify that the booking list ever includes bookings for which the current user is neither organizer nor attendee (or admin/owner), so the failure case isn’t fully provable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The authorization check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, so a user must be BOTH the team admin AND the team owner to satisfy the team-permission branch. Any team admin who is not also the team owner is wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN, and because the same expression is the only team-based path, the gate as written either over-restricts admins or — if someone later 'fixes' the surrounding code — silently widens who can mutate any booking's attendees; as-is it is a broken authorization gate on a mutation that writes to arbitrary bookings and triggers emails/calendar updates.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the team-permission check is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both admin and owner to pass (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`). This will incorrectly reject legitimate team admins who are not also owners with `FORBIDDEN` on the new `addGuests` mutation, which writes to bookings and triggers calendar/email updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The blacklist is lowercased (BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS split and .toLowerCase()) but the incoming guest strings are compared un-normalized, so blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) is a normalization-mismatch bypass. An authorized user adds a guest with mixed case (e.g. 'Blocked@evil.com' against blacklist entry 'blocked@evil.com') and the deny rule never matches; the blacklisted email is enrolled as a booking attendee and receives the full ICS/email payload, defeating the operator-configured blacklist entirely.
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same case-normalization bug: the blacklist entries are lowercased but incoming guest emails are not, so `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` can be bypassed with uppercase/mixed-case emails, defeating BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Existing-attendee dedup uses exact string equality (guest === attendee.email) while emails are not case-normalized anywhere in the schema or handler (ZAddGuestsInputSchema only checks z.string().email()). A guest already on the booking who is re-added with different case ('Jane@Example.com' vs stored 'jane@example.com') bypasses the duplicate filter and is created a second time via createMany, producing duplicate attendees who each get emailed and re-added to the calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, deduplication uses exact string equality (`guest === attendee.email`) when filtering `uniqueGuests`, and neither the input schema (`z.string().email()`) nor the handler normalizes email case. This means an existing attendee `jane@example.com` can be re-added as `Jane@Example.com` and bypass the dedup filter, then be inserted via `attendees.createMany`, creating duplicate attendees for the same logical email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input 'guests' rather than the handler's filtered 'uniqueGuests', and the newGuests.includes(attendee.email) comparison is case-sensitive against un-normalized input. Attendees whose emails differ in case (or duplicates filtered server-side) are misclassified into the wrong email template: an existing attendee gets the 'new guest' full AttendeeScheduledEmail and a newly added guest gets only the 'guests added' notice without the full booking details; who gets bitten is every recipient of a guest-added email where case drifts between input and stored attendee records.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, guests are filtered into `uniqueGuests` for DB insertion (`guestsFullDetails` derived from `uniqueGuests`), but the email dispatch uses the original unfiltered `guests` (`await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`). In `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` classifies recipients via `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, which is case-sensitive and assumes `newGuests` matches the final added set. Passing raw input means (a) emails that were filtered out server-side (already-attendees / blacklisted) can still be treated as “new” and get `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, and (b) case differences between input and stored attendee emails can cause newly added guests to be misclassified and receive the wrong template. This misclassification is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails is wrapped in try/catch that swallows the error with a bare console.log of a static string, discarding the err object. Operators debugging why guests received no confirmation email have no error detail in logs (the thrown error is dropped, not logged), and the mutation still returns success, so failures are silent to both the user and the log trail.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that catches `err` but only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log/propagate the error. The handler then still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, making email delivery failures silent to both logs (no error detail) and the caller (mutation still succeeds). This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/UX issue, though not necessarily a hard correctness defect if email sending is intended to be best-effort.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The attendee-createMany and the downstream calendar/email side effects run non-atomically: prisma.booking.update commits new attendee rows before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendieves and sendAddGuestsEmails execute, with no transaction and no compensating delete. When updateCalendarAttendees throws (bad credential, calendar API failure) the handler rejects with a 500 but the guest rows are already persisted — bookings show guests who were never added to the external calendar event or emailed, and there is no remove-guests endpoint to undo them, so the data drift is permanent without manual SQL.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the DB write happens first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and is committed before the external side effects (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and then `sendAddGuestsEmails`). There is no `prisma.$transaction` wrapping these steps and no compensating rollback/delete if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws. Since `updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited outside any try/catch, a failure will reject the handler (500) after guests are already persisted, leaving the booking showing added guests even though calendar update (and potentially emails) did not complete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New attendee rows are created with name: "" and the guest's locale/timeZone copied from the organizer rather than the guest, bypassing the enrichment/validation the booking flow normally applies. Organizers receive calendar invites and emails addressing guests as empty names, and any downstream code that renders attendee names (ICS attendee CN, email templates) shows blank strings for every guest added through this path.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new attendee records are created with `name: ""` and `timeZone`/`locale` copied from the organizer (`guestsFullDetails` uses `organizer.timeZone`/`organizer.locale`). The resulting `CalendarEvent` attendees list is built from these persisted attendees and is then used for calendar updates and email generation (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`), so downstream templates/ICS that use attendee `name` will see blank strings for guests added via this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] isTeamAdminOrOwner computes (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)), requiring the caller to be BOTH admin AND owner rather than either, so plain team admins are denied. A team admin who is not the team owner attempts to add guests to a team booking they do not organize and receives FORBIDDEN despite being an admin — the authorization gate silently rejects a class of users the UI's add_members menu item is shown to.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and the team owner. This will incorrectly deny access to team admins who are not owners, and because the authorization gate is `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`, those admins will be blocked from adding guests. This is directly verifiable from the diff; the expected logic for an "admin or owner" check would be `||`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails failures are caught and reduced to console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") without the err object, then the handler returns success. When the email service fails, the API returns {message:"Guests added"} and the UI shows a success toast while no organizer or attendee ever receives a notification email; the error variable isn't even logged, so the failure is unobservable in production logs and permanently swallowed.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try { ... } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless. This makes email-notification failures silently swallowed (no `err` logged), while the API/UI will still report success, so missing notifications become unobservable and unrecoverable from the caller’s perspective.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Attendees are committed to the database (prisma.booking.update createMany) before updateCalendarAttendees and email sending run, with no rollback or compensation if either later step throws. If eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees throws (bad credential, calendar API error), the request 500s but the guests rows are already persisted; the calendar event never gains the guests and no email is sent, while the database says they were added — silent partial state with no retry path, since a retry hits the duplicate-filter and returns BAD_REQUEST.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler persists new attendee rows first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` and then attempts email sending. There is no transaction/rollback or compensating logic if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (it is not wrapped in try/catch). In that failure case, the request will error after the DB has been updated, leaving guests stored in Prisma but not applied to the external calendar and (since execution stops) no emails sent. A retry will compute `uniqueGuests` by filtering out existing attendees and can hit `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and throw BAD_REQUEST, matching the finding’s “no retry path” claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The dedup filter compares guest emails to existing attendees but never dedups within the input array itself (the uniqueness refine exists only in the client-side schema in AddGuestsDialog.tsx; ZAddGuestsInputSchema in addGuests.schema.ts has no uniqueness check), so duplicate guests in one request are createMany'd twice. A client that bypasses the dialog (or any direct tRPC caller) sending guests:["a@x.com","a@x.com"] creates two duplicate Attendee rows for the same booking and sends the guest two confirmation emails; the booking then permanently shows duplicated attendees.
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes that the server-side logic filters out existing/blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate repeated emails within the same request, leading createMany to insert duplicate attendee rows (and even duplicate emails being sent). This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When uniqueGuests.length === 0 after filtering, the handler throws TRPCError BAD_REQUEST "emails_must_be_unique_valid", but that condition also covers the case where every requested guest already exists as an attendee. A user who retries after a partially-failed earlier request (attendees persisted, calendar/emails failed — see the no-rollback finding) gets 'emails must be unique and valid' even though their input is perfectly valid and unique; the wrong-shape, wrong-content error misdirects debugging and blocks the retry that would be needed to complete the calendar update and emails.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails that already exist in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted ones. If the caller submits only emails that are already attendees (a valid, unique input), `uniqueGuests.length === 0` triggers `throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, which is a misleading error message for that case. However, the diff doesn’t establish expected idempotent retry semantics (i.e., whether re-adding existing guests should succeed), so it’s best framed as an edge-case/UX/API contract issue rather than a strictly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), so it is true only for users who are simultaneously admin AND owner — a team admin who is not the owner is denied, and isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0) is also evaluated for personal bookings where teamId is null. Team admins (not owners) who should be permitted to manage guests on team bookings get FORBIDDEN, and for every non-team booking the handler still runs two team-membership queries against teamId 0 on the hot path; the authorization gate does not match its evident intent (admin OR owner).

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`, which requires the user to be both admin AND owner. The subsequent auth gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` will incorrectly deny team admins who are not owners. Additionally, for non-team bookings (`teamId` null/undefined), both membership checks are still executed against `teamId ?? 0`, causing unnecessary queries and potentially unintended semantics for teamId 0.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Blacklist comparison lowercases the env-var entries but compares them against guest emails verbatim, so 'User@Example.com' does not match a blacklisted 'user@example.com'. Any guest email with different letter casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entirely and is added to the booking; the blacklist the operator configured silently fails to block, with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the comparison uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where `guest` is taken verbatim from input (`guests`). Since `guest` is not lowercased, a differently-cased email (e.g., `User@Example.com`) will not match a blacklisted `user@example.com` and will bypass the blacklist and be added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The EventManager is constructed with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) — the requesting user's credentials — rather than the booking organizer's (booking.user.credentials is even fetched in the findFirst include and then unused). When an attendee or team admin adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs against apps the organizer's calendar lives on but with the requester's (possibly empty) credential set, so the organizer's calendar event is never updated with the new guests and the failure is invisible because the handler still returns success.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation allows non-organizers (team admin/owner, or an attendee) to add guests, but constructs `EventManager` with the **requesting** user and their credentials (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` then `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`). Meanwhile the booking query includes `booking.user.credentials` but those organizer credentials are never used. If the organizer’s calendar integrations/credentials differ from the requester’s (or requester has none), `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` may not update the organizer’s external calendar event even though guests are persisted in DB and the handler returns success (errors are not surfaced; only email sending is wrapped in try/catch). This is a concrete, diff-grounded correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The onError toast builds `"${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}"`, a template literal that is always truthy, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never render and err.data?.code renders as the literal string 'undefined' when code is absent. Users see toasts like 'undefined: booking_not_found' — the server's raw translation key shown untranslated alongside 'undefined', misdirecting the user; the intended human-readable fallback is dead code.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the onError handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal always yields a truthy string (even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined`), so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is effectively dead code. This can also surface as user-facing toasts like `"undefined: ..."` when `err.data?.code` is absent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Closing the dialog via Dialog onOpenChange (clicking the backdrop or Escape) resets neither multiEmailValue nor isInvalidEmail, unlike the Cancel button which resets both. A user who triggers the validation error, closes the dialog via backdrop/Escape, and reopens it sees the stale red 'Emails must be unique and valid' error and their previous emails with no way to realize the state wasn't fresh; two close paths have drifted apart.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, the Dialog uses `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` so closing via backdrop/Escape only toggles `isOpenDialog` and does not reset local state. The only reset logic (`setMultiEmailValue([""])` and `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`) is inside the Cancel button onClick. Therefore, after a validation error, closing the dialog via backdrop/Escape and reopening will preserve stale `multiEmailValue` and the red error state, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] replyTo is built by appending the organizer email plus every attendee email with no bound, so the header grows linearly with attendee count. On bookings with many attendees (large seat-based bookings, or after repeated addGuests calls), the reply-to header exceeds SMTP recipient header limits and the receiving server rejects or truncates the message, silently failing delivery of the organizer notification.

adjudication.rationale: The new email template `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts` sets `replyTo` to an array containing the organizer email plus *all* attendee emails: `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`. Since `attendees` can grow via repeated `addGuests` calls (see `addGuests.handler.ts` creating new attendees), the Reply-To header size grows linearly with attendee count and is unbounded in this diff. That can cause email delivery failures if header/address limits are exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ZAddGuestsInputSchema puts no cap on the guests array length, and the handler issues one calendar-attendee update plus one email per guest with no bound. A single authenticated request with hundreds of guest emails fans out to hundreds of SMTP sends and calendar-API attendee updates from one mutation, an amplification vector that also slows the request until SMTP timeouts surface as the swallowed-email failure above; the parallel client-side schema in AddGuestsDialog.tsx duplicates the same array schema, so the two validators will drift.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `addGuests` with `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` allowing an unbounded `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` (no `.max(...)`). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation can create many attendees (`createMany`) and then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` with the full attendee list, and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which fans out `sendEmail` calls across `calendarEvent.attendees` plus organizer/team-member notifications—so a single request can trigger hundreds of downstream calendar/SMTP operations (DoS/amplification risk). Also, the client duplicates a similar but not identical schema in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` (adds a uniqueness refine) while the server schema lacks that constraint, creating drift/inconsistent validation behavior.
